name: OriginMark AI
author: mnecas

sections.description:
OriginMark AI lets you clearly disclose which content on your website was created with the help of AI. Mark an image as AI-generated from the Media Library, and the plugin automatically overlays a small “AI Generated” badge on it wherever it appears on your live site — no manual editing of your content required.

You can also mark posts and pages whose text was written with AI. Choose “Created with the help of AI” or “Generated by AI” in the editor, and readers will see a short notice above or below the content.

Features

  • Mark any image as AI-generated directly from the Media Library.
  • Mark or unmark many images at once with bulk actions, see which images are marked in the “AI” column and filter the Media Library to AI-generated images only.
  • Automatically displays an “AI Generated” badge on marked images anywhere they appear in your content.
  • Choose between white, black, or white-transparent badge styles.
  • Configure badge size, corner position, and edge offset.
  • Mark posts, pages or other content types as created with the help of AI or generated by AI, in both the block editor and the classic editor.
  • Show a notice to readers above or below the content, with customizable texts, or place it yourself with the [originmark_ai_notice] shortcode or the originmark_ai_notice() template function.
  • No changes to your existing images or media files — the badge is added dynamically on output.

Why disclose AI-generated content?

Transparency around AI-generated content can help visitors understand how content on your website was created. In certain circumstances, EU law may require AI-generated or AI-manipulated content to be clearly disclosed. OriginMark AI provides a simple, non-destructive way to add a visible label to content you identify as AI-generated.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/originmark-ai directory, or install the plugin directly through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings > OriginMark AI to choose your badge style, size, position, and offset.
  4. Open any image in your Media Library, check the “AI Generated” checkbox, and save.
  5. The badge will automatically appear on that image wherever it’s used in your published content.
  6. To mark text, open a post or page and choose an option in the “AI content” panel (block editor sidebar or classic editor box).
sections.faq:
Does this modify or overwrite my original image files?

No. The badge is added dynamically to the HTML output when the page is displayed — your original image files are never modified.

Where does the badge appear?

In post content and, by default, also outside it: featured images, images your theme outputs with wp_get_attachment_image(), WooCommerce product images and image blocks in block theme templates. You can turn off labels outside post content in Settings > OriginMark AI if they conflict with your theme, a slider or a lightbox. Badges are not added to feeds or REST API responses; headless sites can read the _originmark_ai_generated field on media items instead.

The badge breaks my theme’s card layout. What can I do?

Images that take their height from their container (for example height: 100% or Tailwind’s h-full) are detected automatically. If your theme sets this in its stylesheet instead, add this CSS to your theme (adjust the selector to your card):

.your-card-image .originmark-wrapper { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; }

Theme developers can also add the originmark-wrapper--fill class with the originmark_wrapper_classes filter, which receives the wrapper classes and the image HTML. You can also turn off labels outside post content in Settings > OriginMark AI.

How do I mark many images at once?

Open Media > Library in list view, select the images, choose Mark as AI generated from the Bulk actions menu and click Apply. The “AI” column shows which images are marked, and the “AI generated only” filter lists just those. Bulk actions are available in list view only, not in grid view.

How do I mark AI-written text?

Open a post or page and find the “AI content” panel in the editor sidebar. Choose “Created with the help of AI” or “Generated by AI” and update the post. A notice appears on the single post view and in RSS feeds. In Settings > OriginMark AI you can choose the content types, the notice position and the notice texts.

Can I place the text notice myself?

Yes. Set the notice position to “Do not insert automatically” and use the [originmark_ai_notice] shortcode in your content, or <?php originmark_ai_notice(); ?> in your theme templates. Use originmark_get_ai_notice() to get the HTML as a string.

Can I use a custom badge icon?

Not yet — the plugin currently ships with three built-in badge styles (white, black, white-transparent). Custom icon uploads may be added in a future release.

Will this plugin support marking AI-generated text in the future?

Yes, this is planned. The current release focuses on images.
sections.changelog:
1.4.0

  • New: mark posts, pages and other content types as created with the help of AI or generated by AI (block editor panel and classic editor box).
  • New: AI notice for readers above or below the content and in RSS feeds, with customizable texts.
  • New: [originmark_ai_notice] shortcode and originmark_ai_notice() / originmark_get_ai_notice() template functions.

1.3.2

  • New: bulk actions to mark or unmark images as AI generated in the Media Library (list view).
  • New: “AI” column and “AI generated only” filter in the Media Library (list view).

1.3.1

  • Fix: badge could be clipped in some browsers (notably Safari) inside animated or masked containers. The drop shadow under the badge was removed; use the white or black badge style for better contrast on busy images.

1.3.0

  • New: badges on featured images, images output by themes via wp_get_attachment_image(), WooCommerce product images and image blocks in block theme templates.
  • New: setting to turn off badges outside post content.
  • Change: badges are no longer added to REST API responses.
  • New: images that fill their container (height: 100%, h-full) keep their layout; new originmark_wrapper_classes filter for theme developers.

1.2.0

  • Refactor: plugin code reorganized into namespaced classes.
  • Change: badge styles moved from inline styles to a stylesheet. CSS classes renamed: .ai-image-wrapper is now .originmark-wrapper, .ai-badge-svg is now .originmark-badge.
  • Change: settings are stored in a single option; existing settings are migrated automatically.
  • New: all plugin data is removed when the plugin is deleted.

1.1.0

  • Fix: an image used more than once in a post no longer gets a duplicate badge.
  • Fix: badge wrapper no longer breaks elements, paragraphs or left/right/center alignment.
  • Fix: the “AI Generated” checkbox is shown only for images.
  • Security: saving the checkbox now relies only on the core attachment save flow with a capability check.
  • Change: the AI flag is stored under a prefixed meta key; existing data is migrated automatically.
  • Requires PHP 8.1 or newer.

1.0

  • Initial release.
